app.title: NEURO-RX Drug Response Prediction Engine
app.summary: The person picks a compound from a sidebar. For that compound the interface matches drug-response values to gene expression across cell lines and splits the cell lines into training and held-out test sets. On the training set it correlates every gene with response and applies false-discovery correction. A volcano plot shows each gene's correlation and significance, with count cards beside it, and the gene table can be exported. Further tabs show the distribution of response values with the most sensitive cell lines, a random-forest model trained on the top genes with its cross-validated and held-out scores, and a predicted-vs-actual plot. A simulator lets the person pick one held-out cell line and compare its predicted response with the measured one.

task.text: Find genes whose expression correlates with sensitivity to a chosen drug, and test how well those genes predict response in held-out cell lines.

data.text: A gene-by-cell-line expression matrix joined to one log IC50 drug-response value per cell line and drug; from these the interface derives per-gene correlation statistics.
data.item: a cancer cell line with its gene expression profile and its log IC50 for one drug

stage.text: analysing public drug-screen and expression data to find candidate response biomarkers and test a predictive model

mechanism.text: One compound chosen in the sidebar drives a gene-level pipeline that feeds four tabs: a volcano scatter with count cards and a CSV export, a response histogram with a top-sensitive table, a model tab with score metrics, a predicted-vs-actual scatter and a per-cell-line prediction picker, and a methods panel listing the significant genes.

field.text: biomarker discovery and drug-sensitivity prediction from cell-line pharmacogenomics in cancer biology

workflow.name: find features associated with an outcome and test a model built on them

steps.here: A 'Target Compound' select box in the sidebar. It defaults to the drugs present from a preset list. Choosing one re-runs the matching of response to expression.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Cell lines are split 80/20 before any testing. On the training set each gene's Pearson r with log IC50 is computed, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR applied. A gene counts as significant when FDR < 0.05 and |r| > 0.2.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A volcano plot of correlation against -log10 raw p, with dashed threshold lines, significant genes coloured, and gene names on hover. Cards beside it count the genes scanned, the significant biomarkers and the train/test cell lines.
A histogram of log IC50 across all matched cell lines, and a table of the ten most sensitive ones.

steps.step: fit a model and check it on held-out items
steps.here: A random forest is trained on up to 20 of the top genes, ranked by FDR. Metric tiles show its 5-fold CV R² on the training set and its test R² and RMSE. A scatter of predicted vs actual on the test set has an OLS trendline.
The 'Cell Line ID' picker chooses a held-out cell line and shows its actual and predicted log IC50, with the error as a delta.
'EXPORT BIOMARKERS' downloads the full gene statistics table as biomarkers.csv. The integrity tab lists the top FDR-significant genes.

distinctive: The train/test split happens before any statistical testing, and FDR, imputation medians and feature selection all use the training partition only, to avoid leakage.
Significance needs both FDR < 0.05 and an absolute correlation above 0.2, so the volcano plot uses correlation in place of fold change.
Model quality is reported twice: as cross-validated R² on the training set and as R² and RMSE on the held-out cell lines.
A per-item simulator sets one held-out cell line's predicted response against its measured one.
